scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “A Nearly Quartic Separation Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity” (preprints/A-Nearly-Quartic-Separation-Between-Randomized-and-Quantum-Query-Complexity-October-5-2026/quartic-query-separation.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 284 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a99f1c38d086a335), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The optimal power is αtot = 4. More precisely, R(f) = O((1 + Q(f))4) for every total Boolean function. For each fixed integer k ≥ 2, there are positive constants ck, Ck, bk and total Boolean functions Fk,m, for all sufficiently large powers of four m, such that Q(Fk,m) ≤ Ck √ m (log m)bk , R(Fk,m) ≥ ck m2−1/k (log m)2 .
